definition: Media content (images, audio, video, or text) that has been generated or significantly altered using AI, as opposed to being captured directly from the real world.
details: Synthetic media spans both benign creative applications and more concerning uses like deepfakes, and its rapid growth has driven increased interest in provenance tracking and content authentication standards.

explainer.lead: Synthetic media is image, audio, video, or text content generated or substantially altered by AI rather than captured from the world. It matters because the same tools serve creative work and convincing deepfakes.

tiers.eli5: It's pictures, voices, or videos made or changed by a computer instead of filmed or recorded for real.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build generators and detectors and increasingly attach provenance metadata; the pitfall is that authentication is only as good as adoption, since unlabelled content circulates freely.
tiers.paperLevel: Synthetic media is defined by origin rather than format — AI-generated or significantly AI-altered — so detection and provenance standards, not a formula, are the operative technical tools.

explainer.example: A marketing video voiced by a cloned avatar and a politician's fabricated speech clip are both synthetic media, distinguished by intent and labelling rather than by the underlying generation method.
